analogs.covers: Body and nights: a small nocturnal browser of coast and island scrub that escapes by speed
Society: a colony of loners, each guarding its own little patch beside the neighbours

headline: A quokka colony where every neighbour guards its own little patch like a pika.

setting.label: Coasts, island scrub and forest edges
setting.note: Nocturnal, though it can switch to a daytime rhythm inside mixed-species herds. The profile map marks coastal, island and forest-edge areas.

playsLike: You are a small nocturnal herbivore living in a large colony, yet each Camptosaurus is really a loner holding its own small home range next to the neighbours'. You rarely interact outside courtship, nesting and border disputes. Only one of you engages a threat, and you flee Achillobator and every Large or bigger carnivore. Your stamina carries you far (sprint 1,125 for 250 s), and you remember faces, places and sounds.

why.text: Lives in large colonies, but each individual keeps a home range that borders the others' and rarely interacts with them. Pikas live exactly like this, each defending its own patch inside the colony (official inspiration).
Small, nocturnal, eats berries but anything else too, and escapes by running. That is the quokka and wallaby lifestyle (official inspiration).
Flighty/Defensive with only 1 engaging (a male may defend a female raising his young). Flees Achillobator and Large+ carnivores.
Recalls locations, sounds and faces, which offsets its motion-based eyesight when spotting danger.
Harem bonds: a male defends the female raising his offspring.

notLike: Quokkas are famously unafraid of people; Camptosaurus is a nervous prey animal.
Pikas live in mountain rock fields, not on coasts.
